summary: Hangzhou suits scenic, slower-paced travel built around lake views, tea culture, elegant old streets, and soft day-to-evening transitions.
transport_notes: Keep West Lake and nearby neighborhoods grouped on the same day to reduce repeated transfers.
Metro plus short walks works well for central Hangzhou, but lake-edge strolling should be left with enough free time.
Romantic or photo-focused plans work best when afternoons and evenings stay near waterfront or historic street areas.

budget_notes.low: Focus on public lakefront spaces, classic streets, and simple local food stops.
budget_notes.medium: Blend West Lake highlights, one cultural stop, and one atmospheric dining or tea area each day.
budget_notes.high: Add slower comfort-oriented pacing, lake-view dining, and more refined tea or boutique street experiences.

trip_type_notes.student: Student trips in Hangzhou should emphasize walkable lake views, affordable food, and photogenic free public spaces.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should feel reflective, easy to navigate, and rich in city scenery without overloading the day.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should emphasize lakefront atmosphere, tea-scented calm, evening reflections, and romantic photo moments.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should avoid overlong walking loops and favor calm, scenic, low-stress areas.
